name: Match famous correspondents to Economist counts

description: Baseline: current correspondace.py reparses normalized headers, matches hand-picked Jeffrey aliases and candidate name_key combinations, and scores against famous_correspondents.csv.

asi.hypothesis: Baseline current heuristic matcher to establish combined_error before iterating.
observations: Very close on Larry Summers, Michael Wolff, Thomas Pritzker, Steve Bannon.
Largest misses are Ariane de Rothschild, Elon Musk, Bill Gates, Reid Hoffman, Kathryn Ruemmler, Lawrence Krauss.
Current logic only searches name_key combinations; it barely uses actual email aliases and likely under-covers Jeffrey aliases.
asi.next_action_hint: Improve candidate generation with email-key support and stricter junk/relative filtering for high-error correspondents.

description: Backfill pure-email rows into candidate search by falling back from name_key to an email-derived search_key, and use that same key for Jeffrey alias detection.

asi.hypothesis: Many misses come from rows that only contain an email address; if those rows get searchable keys, undercounted correspondents should recover a chunk of missing volume.
observations: combined_error improved from 3.1006 to 3.0556.
ratio_log_error improved from 1.1703 to 1.1307.

This helps aggregate coverage a bit but does not fix the biggest alias problems; Bill Gates and Elon Musk barely moved, suggesting those are more about bad candidate inclusion/exclusion than missing pure-email rows.
asi.next_action_hint: Inspect the worst correspondents and tighten candidate filters or add person-specific email/domain heuristics for Ariane, Elon, Bill, Reid, Kathryn, and Krauss.

description: Tighten broad include tokens for Ariane, Elon, Kathryn, Krauss, and Bill by removing generic first-name triggers and biasing toward surname/email-domain keys.

asi.hypothesis: Broad include tokens like ariane, elon, bill, and lawrence were pulling in junk candidates, so stricter surname/email-domain matching might cut false positives and improve worst-person fits.
asi.rollback_reason: The stricter filters removed too much useful coverage and made combined_error worse, jumping from 3.0556 to 3.5155 with much larger total delta.
observations: Ariane and other undercounted correspondents appear to need some of the broader aliases or email-only variants after all.
Elon barely improved despite extra Musk-specific filters, so his error is not mainly from the worst broad-token false positives.
Bill Gates selection worsened when generic bill-based support was removed.
asi.next_action_hint: Revert to the previous broader search, then target one person at a time with additive person-specific email aliases instead of globally tightening include rules.

description: Auto-derive extra Jeffrey alias keys from sender rows that use known Jeffrey email addresses, then reuse those learned keys when identifying Jeffrey as recipient/sender.

asi.hypothesis: A lot of undercounted correspondents may be missing because Jeffrey appears under many garbled recipient aliases not covered by the tiny manual alias list.
asi.rollback_reason: The broader Jeffrey alias set reduced total_abs_delta but increased ratio_log_error enough to worsen the primary combined_error from 3.0556 to 3.0791.
observations: This confirms there is missing Jeffrey alias coverage in the data, but naive expansion picks up asymmetrical aliases that distort ratios.
The change likely inflated one side of the exchange graph more than the other.
A more careful approach would learn aliases separately for sender and recipient contexts or require both email-backed evidence and recipient-side frequency.
asi.next_action_hint: Try person-specific fixes next, or learn stronger Jeffrey aliases with stricter filters instead of broad auto-expansion.

description: Try direction-specific matching by choosing sender-side and recipient-side key subsets independently from implied target sent and received counts.

asi.hypothesis: The same alias set is probably not valid in both directions; choosing sender and recipient keys independently should fit asymmetric correspondents like Ariane and Bill much better.
asi.rollback_reason: Searching sender and recipient subsets separately across the full candidate list blew up runtime and hit the experiment timeout before producing metrics.
observations: The idea is still promising, but naive exhaustive search is too expensive at current candidate widths.
Need pruning: smaller candidate lists, top-N per direction, greedy search, or beam search instead of full combinations.
asi.next_action_hint: Prototype a cheaper beam search or cap hard people to a much smaller preferred candidate list before trying directional matching again.

description: Use fast greedy direction-specific key picking to match implied sent and received totals independently instead of forcing one shared key set per person.

asi.hypothesis: A cheap directional picker might capture asymmetric aliases without the runtime blow-up of exhaustive sender/recipient subset search.
asi.rollback_reason: The greedy picker was too myopic and grabbed high-volume junk keys like billconover and jermaine, causing a huge ratio_log_error spike and much worse combined_error.
observations: Greedy direction-specific search is unsafe without stronger candidate gating.
Independent sent/received fitting can easily overfit totals while matching the wrong person entirely.
The idea still seems structurally useful, but it needs very strict person-specific candidate pools or a better scoring function.
asi.next_action_hint: Return to the shared-subset baseline and improve candidate generation/gating before trying directional matching again.

description: Target only a few problem people: add Ariane email aliases to prefer lists and tighten Bill/Reid/Elon candidate includes to reduce generic-name junk.

asi.hypothesis: A small amount of person-specific candidate curation might improve the hardest mismatches without destabilizing the whole matcher.
asi.rollback_reason: The targeted curation still worsened the primary metric, pushing combined_error from 3.0556 to 3.1445 and increasing both ratio and total error.
observations: Bill still picked generic gate/bill-like junk despite tighter includes, so candidate ranking alone is not enough.
Ariane remains the main unsolved structural problem; adding email aliases did not bridge the large missing volume.
Small local tweaks are not beating the baseline shared-subset search.
asi.next_action_hint: Either add stronger per-person candidate gating rules in the actual subset search, or inspect whether the target numbers require message-level deduplication/thread handling rather than only alias tweaks.

description: Bias subset search toward curated aliases by adding a small penalty for picked keys outside each person's prefer list, and promote Ariane email aliases into that preferred set.

asi.hypothesis: The matcher is overfitting with small generic keys; a light penalty on non-preferred aliases should keep the search on cleaner person-specific keys and avoid junk additions like Bill/Gates fragments.
asi.rollback_reason: The preference penalty cleaned up some local choices like Bill Gates, but it worsened overall combined_error from 3.0556 to 3.3022 by preventing useful non-preferred keys elsewhere.
observations: Bill Gates became exact on total but ratio stayed off, so his remaining error is intrinsic to the main billgates bucket, not junk extras.
Ariane email aliases still did not solve the huge missing-volume problem.
Soft alias penalties are too blunt globally.
asi.next_action_hint: If we revisit alias penalties, make them person-specific rather than global; otherwise pivot to a different counting model such as message-level dedupe/directness rules.

description: Test a more direct-exchange counting model by ignoring cc/bcc and only counting sender<->to_recipients links against Jeffrey.

asi.hypothesis: The Economist numbers may be closer to direct exchanges than any-address participation, so dropping cc/bcc could reduce overshoots on Bill, Elon, and Reid.
asi.rollback_reason: The run hit the experiment timeout before producing metrics, so the effect on the primary metric is unknown.
observations: Unexpectedly, this variant was slower enough to time out under the current 120s budget.
Need either a longer timeout for this workload or a quick ad hoc runtime check before retrying.
asi.next_action_hint: If retrying direct-only counting, rerun with a larger timeout or speed up the subset search first.

description: Swap correspondace.py to consume the richer precomputed data/email_addresses.parquet instead of reparsing emails.normalized.parquet in-place.

asi.hypothesis: Using the already repaired parsed-address table from nb.py should recover better display names and email repairs than the lightweight local reparse, potentially improving correspondence matching.
asi.rollback_reason: This was effectively flat to slightly worse than the current best kept metric (3.05895 vs 3.05558), so it does not justify changing the code path.
observations: The richer parsed-address dataset reproduces almost exactly the same scores as the lighter in-file reparse.
That means current mismatch is not mostly from missing address parsing repairs; the remaining gap is in the matching/counting logic.
Runtime improved substantially, which could still matter if we later revisit more expensive search ideas.
asi.next_action_hint: Use the faster parsed-address source as an optional implementation detail only if it enables a stronger search strategy that actually improves combined_error.

description: Replace exhaustive subset search with a fast beam search over up to 18 candidates, using the richer parsed-address table to make broader candidate exploration cheap.

asi.hypothesis: The current exhaustive search is too constrained by a 12-candidate cap; a beam search over a wider candidate pool could find better subsets, especially for hard underfit names.
asi.rollback_reason: Although the primary metric dropped sharply, inspection showed the beam search was matching obviously wrong people like Peter Mandelson for Elon Musk and Ariane Dwyer for Ariane de Rothschild. This is benchmark overfitting, not a valid improvement.
observations: Beam search itself is promising: runtime fell to ~18s and the optimizer found much lower numeric error.
The failure mode is poisoned candidate generation from broad first-name fragments like `erm`, `ariane`, `larry`, and `bill`.
A stricter surname/email-domain candidate gate paired with beam search may be a real path forward.
asi.next_action_hint: Keep the beam-search structure but tighten include tokens for the most toxic names so junk candidates never enter the pool.

description: Retry beam search with junk-resistant include tokens: remove toxic first-name fragments like ariane, larry, lawrence, bill, and erm from candidate generation for the worst overfitting cases.

asi.hypothesis: The beam search itself looked promising, but candidate pools were poisoned by broad first-name fragments; tightening those pools should preserve speed while avoiding bogus matches.
asi.rollback_reason: The stricter candidate pools overshot in the other direction and produced a much worse combined_error of 3.5339.
observations: Beam search without the broad first-name tokens lost too much legitimate coverage for several people.
This suggests the right fix is not just pruning includes globally; it likely needs smarter scoring or person-specific candidate validation.
Parsed-address + beam remains fast, but not yet trustworthy.
asi.next_action_hint: Revert to the kept baseline and either build explicit person-specific allowlists for the problematic names or revisit a counting-model change with a fast implementation.

description: Test a more direct-address counting model on the faster parsed-address source by counting only sender<->to_recipients links and ignoring cc/bcc participation.

asi.hypothesis: The Economist counts may reflect more direct exchanges than any-address participation, so dropping cc/bcc might reduce false-positive volume for famous names without changing the basic alias logic.
asi.rollback_reason: The direct-only model completed quickly but slightly worsened the primary metric from 3.0556 to 3.1057.
observations: This is a useful negative result: the target numbers are not simply explained by excluding cc/bcc.
Bill and Elon changed only modestly, so their mismatch is mostly not a cc/bcc artifact.
Using data/email_addresses.parquet does make these counting-model experiments much faster.
asi.next_action_hint: Keep the baseline counting model. If revisiting counting changes, focus on dedupe or directness filters beyond simple cc/bcc removal.

description: Prioritize matching total emails before ratio inside subset selection, and add a few strongly-evidenced Jeffrey alias variants like jeffepstein/jefffreyepstein/jeevacation.

asi.hypothesis: If subset search picks the closest total first and only then optimizes ratio, it may satisfy the user's instruction and recover the large undercounts on names like Ariane and Krauss; a few extra Jeffrey aliases might help total coverage too.
asi.rollback_reason: Total-first ranking did shrink total_abs_delta sharply, but it blew up ratio error and made the primary combined_error much worse.
observations: This confirms there is a real tradeoff: forcing exact totals encourages clearly wrong directional balance.
The extra Jeffrey aliases were not enough to overcome that tradeoff.
The current benchmark genuinely requires balancing total and ratio jointly even if total is explored first heuristically.
asi.next_action_hint: Keep ratio in the inner objective, but use total-first ideas only as a tie-breaker or in constrained per-person searches where alias pools are trustworthy.
